rot.ideia.ex1.e1: Three rules to start well; I will teach one at a time. The first: take the center.
rot.ideia.ex1.e2: The center is the squares d4, e4, d5 and e5. A piece in the center watches more squares.
rot.ideia.ex1.p: Take the center with a pawn, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex1.certo: That's right! The pawn takes e4 and also opens the way for the bishop and the queen.
rot.ideia.ex1.revela: The king's pawn moves two squares and takes the center.
rot.ideia.ex1.alt.d2d4.1: That is great too! The queen's pawn takes d4.
rot.ideia.ex1.alt.d2d4.2: Look also at the king's pawn on e4.
rot.ideia.ex1.err.a2a4.1: That pawn goes along the edge and does not take the center.
rot.ideia.ex1.err.a2a4.2: Let's go back: look for the squares in the middle of the board.
rot.ideia.ex1.err.h2h4.1: That pawn goes along the edge and does not take the center.
rot.ideia.ex1.err.h2h4.2: Let's go back: look for the squares in the middle of the board.
rot.ideia.ex1.fora: That pawn does not reach the center. Let's go back: look for d4 or e4.
rot.ideia.ex1.volta: Take the center with a pawn, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex1.l1: Remember the first rule: start with the center.
rot.ideia.ex2.e1: The second rule: bring the knights and bishops into play. This is called developing.
rot.ideia.ex2.e2: The knights come out first, and toward the center.
rot.ideia.ex2.certo: That's right! The knight on f3 faces the center and attacks the pawn on e5.
rot.ideia.ex2.revela: The knight goes to f3: it faces the center and attacks the pawn on e5.
rot.ideia.ex2.alt.b1c3.1: That is good too! The knight on c3 also faces the center.
rot.ideia.ex2.alt.b1c3.2: Look also at the knight on f3, which also attacks the pawn on e5.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.g1h3.1: On the edge, the knight watches few squares. It plays better near the center.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.g1h3.2: Let's go back: bring the knight toward the center.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.b1a3.1: On the edge, the knight watches few squares. It plays better near the center.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.b1a3.2: Let's go back: bring the knight toward the center.
rot.ideia.ex2.fora: It comes out too, but the knight plays better facing the center. Let's go back.
rot.ideia.ex2.l1: Remember the second rule: knights and bishops into play, facing the center.
rot.ideia.ex2.l2: Now I will show why the center matters and an opening up to castling.
rot.demos.borda.e1: Compare the knight on the edge and in the center.
rot.demos.borda.l1: On h3, the knight watches only four squares.
rot.demos.borda.l2: On f3, it watches eight squares. That is why the knight goes to the center.
rot.demos.abertura.e1: A healthy opening, from the start to castling.
rot.demos.abertura.l1: First, a pawn in the center.
rot.demos.abertura.l3: Then the knight, facing the center.
rot.demos.abertura.l4: The black knight protects the pawn.
rot.demos.abertura.l5: The bishop comes out and aims at the center and f7, the weak square next to the black king.
rot.demos.abertura.l7: Finally, castling: the king moves two squares and the rook jumps to its other side.
rot.demos.abertura.l8: Now the king sits in the corner, protected by the pawns.
rot.demos.abertura.l9: The third rule: castle early. And do not move the same piece twice without a reason.
rot.demos.abertura.l10: Now it's your turn: start a game with the three rules.
rot.pratica.abertura.enunciado: Start the game: king's pawn to the center, king's knight, king's bishop and castling.
rot.pratica.abertura.fim: Well done. Center, pieces in play and a safe king: the three opening rules.
